nodes.label: LSAT topic bootcamp bootstrap
nodes.summary: Audit-driven bootstrap of a new LSAT U topic bootcamp project: walk the topic corpus, tier-grade it, scan the Mac for stray related files, benchmark quality, then generate the project folder and a Claude Code kickoff prompt. v2 does real Stage-1 audit work up front (~20-40 min) instead of emitting placeholder templates.

nodes.label: S/A/B/C/D corpus tier grading
nodes.summary: Score every source file across 10 rubric dimensions (pedagogical clarity, factual rigor, completeness, tone, voice strength, visual teaching, interaction design, polish, curriculum coherence, uniqueness multiplier) and assign a tier from S (gold standard, preserve verbatim) to D (delete). Uniqueness caps the grade so redundant files cannot score high.

nodes.label: Repetition map / dedupe cluster
nodes.summary: Cluster source files by content overlap, name the cleanest version per cluster, and mark the rest as drops. Feeds the Gate 2 deduplication pass so the same concept is not taught twice from two files.

nodes.label: Per-module gap analysis
nodes.summary: Compare the audited corpus against the candidate six-module bootcamp structure and mark each module sufficient / marginal / insufficient, with a remediation choice (author, defer to v1.5, merge, drop). Prevents claiming a topic has enough material when it does not.

nodes.label: AUDIT_REPORT.md
nodes.summary: The Stage-1 audit deliverable: tier rankings, repetition map, garbage list, Mac-scan results, per-module gap table, named tools, worked examples, traps, opinionated recommendations. Claude Code reads it as the Gate 2 baseline instead of re-auditing, saving ~50% of Gate 1/2 time.

nodes.label: Handoff control document
nodes.summary: The per-project control document Claude Code must read first and restate as an 8-point understanding before acting. Carries the gate structure, source paths, preservation rules, design scouting rules, and the what-must-not-happen list.

nodes.label: Running project-memory ledger
nodes.summary: PROJECT_MEMORY.md: the single source of truth for project state, read at every session start and updated at every gate close. Holds an append-only dated decisions log, rules learned, tools approved/rejected, quality bar, and lessons that bubble back into the skill itself.

nodes.label: Gate-driven blocking approval workflow
nodes.summary: Gate 0 source-access → Gate 1 scaffolding + reference study → Gate 2 content inventory → Gate 3 architecture lock → Gate 4 per-module review → Gate 5 pre-merge. Each gate is explicit, blocking, and requires written sign-off; no production code before Gate 3.

nodes.label: No silent content drops
nodes.summary: The curriculum corpus is the product. Every reviewed source item must land either in the v1 inventory table or on a Not-Included-in-v1 table with a reason; anything on neither is a build failure regardless of UI quality. Enforced by machine-checkable parity artifacts under /docs/parity/.

nodes.label: Silent content drop
nodes.summary: Shipping a beautiful app that quietly loses questions, drills, named tools, voice passages, or reference sections. Named explicitly as the build-failure condition the whole gate + parity apparatus exists to prevent.

nodes.label: Two-register voice preservation
nodes.summary: Register 1 (decisive, verdict-style, procedural) for reference, simulator, drill instructions; Register 2 (whimsical, parodic, metaphor-led) for lessons and drill setup. Named tools keep their exact names; voicy passages ship verbatim; never rewrite into generic editor tone.

nodes.label: Persistence adapter pattern
nodes.summary: App code talks only to a `Persistence` interface, never to localStorage / IndexedDB / Supabase directly. v1 ships LocalStorage + IndexedDB implementations so a future Supabase swap is a one-file change and LSAT U absorption is a layer swap, not a rewrite.

nodes.label: Component scouting: primitives only
nodes.summary: 21st.dev MCP is allowed for primitive components only (buttons, tabs, drawers, badges, rows), never for layout-scale composition; hit rate is about 1 useful primitive per 7 calls and Magic Generate is rejected outright. Layouts come from direct reference apps (Linear, Readwise, Superhuman, Anki, UWorld).

nodes.label: User edits are authoritative
nodes.summary: Rule 14: any file edit or chat override by Joshua must be detected, acknowledged with a JOSHUA OVERRIDE / JOSHUA EDIT callout, logged as a dated row in the decisions log, and treated as authoritative. Conflicts with existing rules are surfaced before proceeding, never silently absorbed.

nodes.label: Ship a review-mode bypass with every gate
nodes.summary: Rule 18: any progressive unlock, LockedRoute, completion prerequisite, or paywall must ship simultaneously with a toggle that opens all gates for pre-ship review. Born from an incident where correct routes looked broken because gating hid them during a walkthrough.

nodes.label: Premium editorial / private-academy aesthetic
nodes.summary: Dark-mode private academy: editorial typography, restrained 1px borders, one warm accent used only on commit/selection, Linear/Arc/Readwise-level density, 150-220ms eased motion with no spring or parallax. The shared quality bar for LSAT U surfaces.

nodes.label: Reject generic AI/SaaS aesthetics
nodes.summary: A rule shared across every UI skill here: no Inter/Roboto defaults, no purple-gradient-on-white, no heavy drop shadows, no gamification or vanity metrics, no AI copywriting cliches. Commit to a specific, intentional aesthetic instead of the model's default.

nodes.label: Minimalist editorial UI protocol
nodes.summary: A prescriptive protocol for warm-monochrome, document-style interfaces: banned element list, named font stacks, exact pastel hex tokens, 1px #EAEAEA borders, bento grids, kbd chrome, and invisible motion via transform/opacity only.

nodes.label: Distinctive frontend design
nodes.summary: Build production-grade web components, pages, and artifacts with a bold committed aesthetic direction chosen before coding. Emphasizes characterful typography, dominant color with sharp accents, unexpected spatial composition, and high-impact orchestrated motion.

nodes.label: Build an MCP server
nodes.summary: Entry point for MCP server development: interrogate the use case, recommend a deployment model, pick a tool-design pattern and framework, scaffold, then test as a custom connector and submit to the directory. Explicitly discovery-first, not code-first.

nodes.label: MCP deployment model selection
nodes.summary: Ranked, opinionated choice between remote streamable-HTTP (default, zero install friction, OAuth works), MCP app with UI widgets, MCPB bundled local, and local stdio (prototypes only). Picking wrong early causes painful rewrites.

nodes.label: Search + execute tool pattern
nodes.summary: For large API surfaces, expose two tools (search_actions, execute_action) with the catalog held server-side, instead of one tool per endpoint. Under ~15 actions, one-tool-per-action wins; a hybrid promotes the 3-5 hottest actions to dedicated tools.

nodes.label: Context window is a public good
nodes.summary: The shared principle behind both tool design and skill authoring: schemas and instructions land directly in the model's context, so every token must justify itself. Assume the model is already smart; add only what it does not know.

nodes.label: Progressive disclosure loading
nodes.summary: Three-level loading: metadata (~100 words, always in context), SKILL.md body (<5k words, loaded on trigger), bundled references and scripts (loaded or executed only when needed). Keeps SKILL.md under ~500 lines by pushing variant detail into references/.

nodes.label: Create or update a skill
nodes.summary: Guide for authoring skills as self-contained folders (SKILL.md + optional scripts/references/assets + agents/openai.yaml UI metadata), including degrees-of-freedom calibration, forward-testing, and a ban on auxiliary README/CHANGELOG clutter.

nodes.label: Frontmatter name+description as the trigger contract
nodes.summary: Only `name` and `description` are read to decide whether a skill fires, so the description must comprehensively state what it does and when to use it. Every SKILL.md in this catalog follows the same contract; optional fields like argument-hint, allowed-tools, and disable-model-invocation tune invocation.

nodes.label: Match degrees of freedom to task fragility
nodes.summary: High freedom (prose heuristics) when many approaches are valid; medium (pseudocode, parameterized scripts) when a preferred pattern exists; low (specific scripts, few parameters) when operations are fragile and a sequence must be followed exactly. A narrow bridge needs guardrails, an open field does not.

nodes.label: Protect validation integrity
nodes.summary: When using subagents to validate a skill, treat them as an evaluation surface: pass raw artifacts and minimum task-local context, never the intended answer, suspected bug, or your prior conclusions. Otherwise you learn only that another agent can reconstruct leaked context.

nodes.label: skills/<name>/SKILL.md invocation layout
nodes.summary: A reference skill demonstrating the user-invoked slash-command layout and its frontmatter options (argument-hint, allowed-tools, model override, $ARGUMENTS), functionally identical to the legacy commands/*.md format.

nodes.label: Split claude/ and codex/ catalog subtrees
nodes.summary: The skill database is inert storage split by tool origin: Claude-sourced skills under claude/, Codex-sourced under codex/, never merged, with vendor items stored as live symlink plus frozen snapshot. Indexed by a shared INDEX.md.

nodes.label: Interview before building
nodes.summary: Batch a set of scoping questions and resolve every branch before producing anything. Appears as build-mcp-server's Phase 1 ('discovery, not code'), the topic builder's single-batch Phase C1 confirmation, and grill-me's relentless plan interview.

nodes.label: Grill me (plan interview)
nodes.summary: A relentless interview that sharpens a plan or design before building. In the Codex catalog it is a thin, model-invocation-disabled shim that delegates to a /grilling session.

nodes.label: MCP auth: CIMD over DCR
nodes.summary: Claude's MCP client supports oauth_dcr, oauth_cimd (preferred for directory entries), Anthropic-held creds, custom_connection, and none; user-pasted bearer tokens are unsupported. Servers must validate token audience (RFC 8707) and never pass tokens through upstream.

nodes.label: Resources, prompts, elicitation, sampling
nodes.summary: The non-tool MCP primitives: resources (host-triggered browsable context), prompts (user slash commands), elicitation (server asks for structured input mid-tool with zero UI code), and sampling (server delegates LLM inference to the host). Elicitation needs a client capability check plus fallback.

nodes.label: Version-sensitive claims ledger
nodes.summary: A references/versions.md file tracking every claim in the skill that depends on a specific SDK, spec, or host version, with instructions for verifying them when the skill is updated. Guards against a skill silently going stale.

nodes.label: LSAT Lab transcription (Claude)
nodes.summary: Drive the open LSAT Lab practice player through a browser and transcribe the full written explanation for every question that has one into a single markdown file per PrepTest, capturing all three explanation styles per question.

nodes.label: LSAT Lab transcription (Codex)
nodes.summary: The Codex port of the same transcription job, with an added execution contract: the in-app Browser only, apply_patch for local edits, a set-log consult step, and a two-source checkpoint between the live question label and the progress file's NEXT pointer.

nodes.label: Verbatim capture, never fabricate
nodes.summary: Accuracy is the entire job: transcribe explanation text word for word, never paraphrase, never invent percentages or question-type tags. Question type is pulled from the Question Details panel rather than inferred.

nodes.label: One markdown file per PrepTest
nodes.summary: Hard output rule: all sections of a PrepTest go in a single organized markdown file with per-question headings, never one file per question or per section, and never a second parallel transcription file.

nodes.label: Progress / resume checkpoint file
nodes.summary: A per-test progress file listing Done, Skipped (video-only), and a NEXT pointer, updated immediately after each validated question capture so a run can be interrupted and resumed without re-doing or skipping work.

nodes.label: Single locked browser surface
nodes.summary: Codex-side rule: use the documented in-app Browser only, never claude-in-chrome, control-chrome, Chrome extensions, or standalone Playwright, and never switch surfaces to work around a connection or auth failure. Stop and report the exact blocker instead.

nodes.label: Chrome DevTools MCP
nodes.summary: The tool layer behind performance tracing and page inspection: performance_start_trace, performance_analyze_insight, list_network_requests, evaluate_script, emulate, list_pages/new_page/navigate_page. Its failures are what the troubleshooting skill exists to diagnose.

nodes.label: Debug and optimize LCP
nodes.summary: Diagnose slow Largest Contentful Paint by recording a trace, analyzing LCP insights, identifying the LCP element and its network timing, then fixing the specific bottleneck subpart. Good is under 2.5s; on 73% of mobile pages the LCP element is an image.

nodes.label: Find the bottleneck before optimizing
nodes.summary: Break the metric into its subparts (TTFB, resource load delay, load duration, render delay) and fix only the dominant one. Compressing an image when render delay is the real bottleneck just shifts the time. The same 'measure first, fix second' rule governs the perf branch of bug diagnosis.

nodes.label: Re-verify the fix under emulation
nodes.summary: Re-run the trace after the change and confirm the bottleneck subpart actually shrank, then re-test under throttled network and CPU (Fast 3G, 4x CPU) because lab conditions hide issues real users hit.

nodes.label: MCP connection troubleshooting wizard
nodes.summary: Step-by-step diagnosis when Chrome DevTools MCP tools or server init fail: locate and read the MCP config, triage known error signatures (DevToolsActivePort, target closed, module not found, flag typos), then consult upstream known-issues docs before changing config.

nodes.label: Read the config before asking or changing it
nodes.summary: First action is to find and interpret the actual configuration file (.mcp.json, .claude/settings.json, .vscode/launch.json) and only ask the user for it if none exists. Then verify with the cheapest probe (list_pages) rather than retrying the original complex command.

nodes.label: Bug diagnosis discipline
nodes.summary: A six-phase discipline for hard bugs and performance regressions: build a feedback loop, reproduce and minimise, hypothesise, instrument, fix with a regression test, then clean up and post-mortem. Phases are skipped only with explicit justification.

nodes.label: Build a tight red-capable feedback loop first
nodes.summary: The core of bug diagnosis: one named command, already run at least once, that is red-capable on this exact symptom, deterministic, fast, and agent-runnable. Ten construction routes are ranked from failing test to HITL script; for flaky bugs the goal is a higher reproduction rate, not a clean repro.

nodes.label: Theorising before a loop exists
nodes.summary: Reading code to build a theory before a red-capable command exists is named as the exact failure the diagnosis skill prevents. Related failure: single-hypothesis generation anchoring on the first plausible idea, countered by producing 3-5 ranked falsifiable hypotheses with stated predictions.

nodes.label: Tagged, removable instrumentation
nodes.summary: Each probe maps to one Phase 3 prediction, one variable changes at a time, debugger beats logs, and every debug log carries a unique prefix like [DEBUG-a4f2] so cleanup is a single grep. Never 'log everything and grep'.

nodes.label: Regression test needs a correct seam
nodes.summary: Write the regression test before the fix, but only where the seam exercises the real bug pattern at the call site. If no correct seam exists, that absence is itself the finding and gets escalated as an architecture problem after the fix lands.

nodes.label: Dispatch parallel agents
nodes.summary: One agent per independent problem domain, all dispatched in a single response so they run concurrently. Each gets specific scope, a clear goal, constraints, and a required output summary; results are then reviewed for conflicts and validated against the full suite.

nodes.label: Constructed, isolated subagent context
nodes.summary: Subagents never inherit the parent session's history; the dispatcher constructs exactly the context they need. This keeps each agent focused and preserves the coordinator's own context for integration work.

nodes.label: Over-broad or unconstrained agent prompt
nodes.summary: 'Fix all the tests' loses the agent; no pasted error context leaves it hunting; no constraints invite a sweeping refactor; no output spec leaves the coordinator blind to what changed. Also a wrong fit when failures are related or state is shared.

nodes.label: Two-axis diff review (standards + spec)
nodes.summary: Review the diff since a pinned fixed point along two deliberately separate axes: does it follow the repo's documented standards, and does it faithfully implement the originating issue or PRD. Each axis runs in its own sub-agent and results are reported side by side, never merged or reranked.

nodes.label: Separate axes so neither masks the other
nodes.summary: Code can follow every standard while implementing the wrong thing, or do exactly what the issue asked while breaking conventions. Keeping the verdicts separate stops a pass on one axis from hiding a failure on the other.

nodes.label: Validate inputs before fanning out
nodes.summary: Confirm the fixed point resolves and the diff is non-empty before spawning sub-agents; verify every source path exists at Gate 0 before any build work; stop the booking run when the roster lacks an email. Cheap upfront checks beat failures discovered downstream.

nodes.label: Tracer-bullet vertical slice issues
nodes.summary: Break a plan into independently-grabbable issues that each cut end-to-end through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests) rather than horizontally through one layer. Each slice is demoable on its own; prefactoring goes first; the breakdown is quizzed with the user before publishing.

nodes.label: Project issue tracker
nodes.summary: An issue-tracker workflow doc (docs/agents/issue-tracker.md) plus a triage label vocabulary, provisioned by a setup skill. Both issue publishing and spec-axis review depend on it to fetch or create tickets.

nodes.label: Execute a written plan
nodes.summary: Load a plan file, review it critically and raise concerns before starting, turn items into todos, execute each step exactly with its verifications, then hand off to a branch-finishing skill. Prefers subagent-driven development when subagents are available.

nodes.label: Stop on blockers, never guess
nodes.summary: Halt immediately on a missing dependency, failing test, unclear instruction, or repeated verification failure and ask rather than forcing through. Echoed by the booking-link skill's refusal to invent an address and the transcription skill's refusal to switch browsers around a blocker.

nodes.label: Bootcamp parity audit
nodes.summary: Score a named LSAT U bootcamp against the flagship Intro to LR bootcamp and the shared quality bar, emitting a fixed 5-point delta report (feature, visual, content/pedagogy, data-quality gaps, verdict plus the single highest-leverage fix). Diagnosis only, never builds.

nodes.label: Synthesis docs define 'done'
nodes.summary: Rather than re-reading a 216-file flagship tree each run, the quality-bar, product-spec, and design-system synthesis docs are treated as the source of truth for what shipped quality means; the codebase is spot-checked only where those docs are ambiguous. A missing entity page is itself reported as a gap.

nodes.label: gws CLI
nodes.summary: The Google Workspace CLI binary that every gws-* skill wraps, with a shared syntax (`gws <service> <resource> <method>`), global flags (--format, --dry-run, --sanitize), pagination flags, and OAuth or service-account auth.

nodes.label: gws shared reference
nodes.summary: The single prerequisite doc every generated gws command skill points at for auth, global flags, security rules, and shell quoting gotchas (zsh `!` expansion in sheet ranges, single-quoting JSON payloads). Generated by `gws generate-skills`.

nodes.label: Confirm before write/destructive commands
nodes.summary: Never output secrets; always confirm with the user before executing a write or delete; prefer --dry-run for destructive operations. Each generated write-command skill repeats the caution banner inline.

nodes.label: Create a calendar event
nodes.summary: `gws calendar +insert` with summary, RFC3339 start/end, optional location, description, repeatable attendees, and --meet to attach a Google Meet link. A write command requiring confirmation.

nodes.label: Meeting prep workflow
nodes.summary: `gws workflow +meeting-prep` reads the next upcoming calendar event with its attendees, description, and linked docs. Read-only, so it never needs the write-confirmation gate.

nodes.label: Model Armor content sanitization
nodes.summary: Create a Model Armor template (default preset: jailbreak) whose name is then passed to +sanitize-prompt / +sanitize-response, or used via the global --sanitize flag to screen responses for PII and content safety.

nodes.label: Send a student booking link
nodes.summary: Rebuild the roster, look up the student's email and booking slug, draft the email in Joshua's voice, optionally send after explicit approval, then log both the follow-up loop and the send ledger row. Collapses four hand-orchestrated steps into one run, single student or batch.

nodes.label: Draft by default, send only on explicit go-ahead
nodes.summary: Anything a student or prospect reads is drafted and not sent unless pre-approved and explicitly green-lit; the --draft flag is never omitted on a first pass. A batch is drafted whole and approved once, and never sent on an ambiguous 'yes'.

nodes.label: Generated roster is the only address source
nodes.summary: Emails and booking slugs are read from a regenerated roster, never guessed or derived (the URL slug differs from the folder slug). Missing email, missing pass, exhausted credits, or a backend disagreement all stop the run. Never hand-edit *.generated.md.

nodes.label: Append-only send ledger and open-loops log
nodes.summary: Two append-only surfaces: the per-student open-loops.md carrying the follow-up commitment, and wiki/send-ledger.md answering 'did X get their email'. Status is `drafted` until it actually goes out, and a failed send is logged as a failure rather than as intent.

nodes.label: YouTube transcripts, search, channels, playlists
nodes.summary: One skill covering the whole YouTube surface via TranscriptAPI: transcripts, video and channel search, channel browsing with pagination, playlists, and within-channel search. Not for uploads or account management.

nodes.label: API key setup and credit budgeting
nodes.summary: Requires TRANSCRIPT_API_KEY in the environment, with a documented setup path if unset, and each call costs credits (most operations 1 credit, some channel lookups free) so workflows are ordered to minimize spend.
